description: Daily aggregated health metrics for each network node.
Contains throughput, latency, packet loss, CPU usage, temperature, connected users, errors, bandwidth utilization, and a composite health score.
One row per node per day. Use this table for trend analysis and comparing node performance over time.
Average bandwidth utilization as a percentage of total available capacity.
Average number of users connected to the node during the day.
Average CPU utilization percentage of the node during the day.
Average network latency in milliseconds for the day.
Average packet loss as a percentage (0.0 to 1.0 scale where 0.01 = 1%).
Average operating temperature of the node in degrees Celsius.
Average data throughput in megabits per second for the day.
Composite health score from 0 to 100. Above 75 is healthy, 50-75 is degraded, 25-50 is poor, below 25 is critical.
Maximum recorded latency in milliseconds during the day.
Number of raw telemetry measurements aggregated into this daily record.
Calendar date of the aggregated measurements.
Unique identifier for the network node.
Human-readable name assigned to the network node.
Classification of the network node such as router, switch, access_point, or gateway.
Maximum number of concurrent users connected to the node during the day.
Maximum CPU utilization percentage recorded during the day.
Maximum recorded throughput in megabits per second during the day.
Geographic region code where the node is deployed (e.g. US-EAST, US-WEST, EU-WEST).
Total count of errors reported by the node during the day.
Hardware manufacturer or vendor of the network node.
Daily summary of network outage events aggregated by date.
Includes outage counts, durations, and severity breakdowns.
Use for understanding outage trends and severity distribution over time.
Daily aggregated health metrics for IoT devices connected to the network.
Contains device-level health scores, battery status, signal strength, and connectivity metrics.
Health scores below 50 indicate degraded devices; below 25 is critical.
Maintenance risk assessment for each network node based on age, health trends, and outage history.
Each row represents the current risk profile of a single node.
Risk categories are: critical, high, medium, low. Use this to prioritize preventive maintenance.
Number of days since the node was installed.
Number of days since the last maintenance event on this node.
Whether the node has backup power (UPS or generator). True means it has backup power.
Date the node was originally installed or commissioned.
Computed risk score indicating likelihood of needing maintenance. Higher is worse (0-100).
Unique identifier for the network node.
Human-readable name assigned to the network node.
Classification of the network node such as router, switch, access_point, or gateway.
Average health score of the node over the recent lookback period (0-100).
Number of outage events for this node in the recent lookback period.
Geographic region code where the node is deployed.
Categorical risk label derived from maintenance_risk_score: critical, high, medium, or low.
Current operational status of the node (e.g. active, inactive, maintenance).
Hardware manufacturer or vendor of the network node.
Root cause analysis of network outages with categorized failure reasons.
Includes outage cause, affected node details, duration, and impact metrics.
Use for identifying systemic issues and recurring failure patterns.
Regional-level aggregated network performance metrics.
Summarizes node counts, average health, throughput, latency, and capacity across each region.
Use for comparing network quality and capacity between geographic regions.
Raw event-level IoT telemetry readings from sensors and connected devices.
Contains individual sensor readings including temperature, humidity, signal strength, and battery level.
Use for drilling into specific device events or investigating anomalies at the raw data level.
Raw event-level network outage records with start time, end time, affected nodes, and severity.
Each row represents a single outage incident.
Use for investigating specific outage events or correlating outages with other telemetry.

content: Gold tables contain pre-aggregated daily summaries; silver tables contain event-level records. Use gold for trend analysis, silver for drilling into specific events. The risk_category column in gold_node_maintenance_risk uses values: critical, high, medium, low — always sort by severity (critical first). IoT device health scores range 0-100: below 50 is degraded, below 25 is critical. gold_iot_device_health has daily aggregates; silver_iot_telemetry has raw readings. Health scores in gold_daily_node_health are composite: above 75 is healthy, 50-75 degraded, 25-50 poor, below 25 critical. When comparing regions, use gold_regional_network_summary for high-level views and gold_daily_node_health grouped by region_code for time-series analysis.
